h: רֹאשׁ חֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר, מַאֲמָר ה׳ Rosh Chodesh Adar — Maamar Hei

p: Just as when Av enters we diminish in joy,
so when Adar enters we increase in joy
We must understand the matter of the increased joy in Adar,
וַהֲלֹא חֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר מוּתָּר בְּהֶסְפֵּד וְתַעֲנִית
for is not the month of Adar permitted for eulogy and fasting,
and we say Tachanun in it?
But the essence of joy is
כְּשֶׁמְּקַבֵּל עָלָיו הַיִּשְׂרָאֵל עֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם
when the Jew accepts upon himself the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven,
and when he is bound to the root, in Hashem Yisbarach;
that is, when he recognizes that Hashem made us,
"The children of Tziyon will exult in their King" (Tehillim ibid.):
when they accept the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven they exult,
הֶפֶךְ עֹל בָּשָׂר וָדָם שֶׁהוּא לְעֹל.
the opposite of the yoke of flesh and blood, which is a burden.
He saw that he was very merry,
אֲמַר וְגִילוּ בִּרְעָדָה כְּתִיב [תְּהִלִּים ב, יא] וְכוּלֵּי
and said, "It is written, 'Rejoice with trembling' (Tehillim 2:11)..."
אֲמַר לֵיהּ בְּכָל עֶצֶב יִהְיֶה מוֹתָר
He said to him, "'In all sadness there is profit'
He said to him, "I am wearing tefillin."
Seemingly the answer is not understood.
But it is because at the time he puts on tefillin
he bears upon himself the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven,
and also the tefillin of the head, which allude
to the aspect of Keser Elyon,
which is the "skull of the tefillin,"
and indicates that the Jew is bound to the root;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר יִשְׂמַח יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּעוֹשָׂיו וְגוֹמֵר בְּמַלְכָּם.
as it says, "Let Yisrael rejoice in its Maker... in their King."
"He made us and we are His...";
וְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק א קכ, ב)
and it is brought in the holy Zohar (I, 120b):
"It is written with an aleph and read with a vav..."
That is, what they interpreted, "Hu made us,"
is that it alludes to the Hidden Atika,
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רצ, א)
And this is what is said, "and to the Aleph are we,"
as they said in the holy Zohar:
"Lo with an aleph — a higher place still."
That is, Aleph, the supernal Pele,
meaning that Yisrael are bound to the root,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה בָּא הַשִּׂמְחָה וּרְנָנָה.
and through this come joy and song.
For this reason they expounded in the Sifrei (Behaaloscha 19):
"And on the day of your rejoicing" (Bamidbar 10:10)
For on Yom Tov there is a mitzvah of joy,
which is not so on Shabbos,
which has no mitzvah of "and you shall rejoice";
רַק הַיִּשְׂרָאֵל כְּשֶׁמְּקַבֵּל עֹל מַלְכוּתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
rather, when the Jew accepts the yoke of His Kingship, Yisbarach,
עַל יְדֵי זֶה יִשְׂמְחוּ בְמַלְכוּתְךָ וְכוּלֵּי
through this "they rejoice in Your Kingship...";
גַּם בְּשַׁבָּת יֵשׁ בּוֹ הִתְגַּלּוּת עַתִּיקָא
Also, on Shabbos there is the revelation of Atika,
that Yisrael are bound to the root,
and then joy comes of itself.
This is what they said in the Gemara (Taanis ibid.):
"Therefore... let him present himself in Adar,
the holy Mazla, that is, Atika,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג עט, ב)
as they said in the holy Zohar (III, 79b):
וַתִּתְפַּלֵּל עַל ה׳ [שְׁמוּאֵל א א, י]
because children depend on the holy Mazla;
וְכֵן הַשְׁלֵךְ עַל ה׳ יְהָבְךָ [תְּהִלִּים נה, כג]
and likewise "Cast your burden upon Hashem" (Tehillim 55:23);
That is, the upper tip of the yud
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג סה, ב)
וְהוּא מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בִּגְמָרָא (שַׁבָּת קנו, א)
And it is what they said in the Gemara (Shabbos 156a):
for the attribute of Ayin, the Hidden Atika,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב סד, ב)
as they said in the holy Zohar (II, 64b),
that is, that they are bound to the root,
the soul of the father is the mazal of the son.
And this is "Hu made us, and to the Aleph are we,"
and then we increase in joy.
The meaning of "his mazal is strong"
מוֹרֶה שֶׁהוּא חָזָק וְדָבָר קַיָּם לָעַד
indicates that it is strong, a thing enduring forever,
from the expression "their strength is firm (bari ulam)" (Tehillim 73:4).
That is, this month is the time
to merit this aspect, that it be forever:
"The lip of truth shall be established forever."
This is what it says in Sefer Yetzirah,
שֶׁחֹדֶשׁ אֲדָר נוֹצַר בְּאוֹת ק׳ בִּשְׂחוֹק.
that the month of Adar was formed with the letter kuf, with laughter.
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בִּגְמָרָא (שַׁבָּת קד, א)
This is according to what they said in the Gemara (Shabbos 104a):
שֶׁרוֹמֵז שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל קְשׁוּרִים בַּשֹּׁרֶשׁ בְּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ
which alludes that Yisrael are bound to the root in Hashem Yisbarach.
and the crown of the yud
alludes to the Mazla of Ayin,
which is Keser Elyon, as was said.
וּבְחֹדֶשׁ זֶה נוֹלַד מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
And in this month Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, was born,
that when he was born the whole house was filled with light;
for he brought down the Torah,
and the Torah emerged from Chochmah,
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב קכא, א)
and the five times "light" in this utterance
correspond to the five Chumashim of the Torah
and it is called "the Torah of Moshe" (Malachi 3:22).
And Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, is the first
in connection with whom holiness of place is mentioned, at the Bush.
into all the souls of Yisrael at Matan Torah,
And in Nissan, as they said
a maidservant saw at the Sea
that is, they merited the revelation of Atika.
And the month of Adar is the preparation for this.
This is what is said regarding Adar (Esther 8:16):
for the essence of joy is when we merit
the light of the yud, Chochmah, from "Let there be light,"
וְקוֹצָא דִּלְעֵילָּא כֶּתֶר עֶלְיוֹן כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
and the upper tip, Keser Elyon, as mentioned above.
And in the Gemara (Megillah 16b) they expounded:
דִּכְשֶׁזּוֹכִין לַתּוֹרָה זוֹכִין לָאוֹר כִּי טוֹב
for when we merit Torah we merit the light "that it was good,"
for the light "that it was good" shines forth in it.
that just as in Av we diminish joy,
so when Adar enters we increase in joy.
טֵית נְהִירוּ דְּחַיִּין בְּכָל אֲתַר וְכוּלֵּי
"Tes is the light of life in every place...;
this letter differs from the letter kuf:
kuf does not settle at all in its place,
and your sign is, 'A slanderous man
shall not be established in the land' (Tehillim 140:12);
אָת ט׳ אִתְיַישְּׁבָא בְּכָל דּוּכְתָּא וְכוּלֵּי
the letter tes settles in every place...;
כְּמָה דְּאָת דָּא שָׁלְטָא בַּאֲתַר דָּא
just as this letter rules in this place,
הָכִי נַמֵּי שָׁלְטָא אָת אַחֲרָא בַּאֲתַר דְּגֵיהִנֹּם
so too another letter rules in the place of Gehinnom:
And in Sefer Yetzirah it states
that Av was formed with the letter tes
and Adar with the letter kuf.
וְהָעִנְיָן בָּזֶה עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמַרְנוּ
The matter is according to what we said
in resolving the question of the Ritva, of blessed memory,
רָאוּ כְּרוּבִין הַמְעוֹרִין זֶה בָּזֶה וְכוּלֵּי
they saw the Keruvim intertwined with one another..."
He asked from what we say (Bava Basra 99a),
that when they do not do the will of the Omnipresent,
and the same applies to the ornamental Keruvim,
that they would show them the ornamental Keruvim:
If so, at the time of the Destruction,
שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ עוֹשִׂין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם
when they were not doing the will of the Omnipresent,
אֵיךְ רָאוּ אוֹתָם מְעוֹרִין זֶה בָּזֶה.
how did they see them intertwined with one another?
And we said that immediately at the time of the Destruction,
when Yisrael saw that enemies had entered the Heichal,
which they had not believed beforehand,
and Yisrael immediately came to be
in the category of those who do His will, Yisbarach;
and the Keruvim became intertwined with one another,
וּבִירוּשַׁלְמִי (בְּרָכוֹת פֶּרֶק ב הֲלָכָה ד יז, ב)
it states that on Tishah b'Av, on the day of the Destruction,
and this is for the reason mentioned above.
Only, it was not yet the time
for the rectification to be complete,
אֲבָל עַל כָּל פָּנִים הָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל
but at any rate Yisrael were
in the category of doing the will of the Omnipresent.
וְזֶהוּ שֶׁנּוֹצַר חֹדֶשׁ אָב בְּאוֹת ט׳
This is why the month of Av was formed with the letter tes,
which is "the light of life in every place,"
from the light "that it was good,"
for then the light truly shone.
And the month of Adar was formed with the letter kuf,
which rules in the place of Gehinnom,
which is darkness and the shadow of death;
אֲבָל הוּא רַק חֹשֶׁךְ לְפוֹשְׁעֵי עוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים וּמַזָּלוֹת
but it is darkness only for the sinners of the idolatrous nations,
and even at the entrance of Gehinnom
which is not so for the sinners of Yisrael,
who, as soon as they come to Gehinnom, instantly
and extinguish the fire of Gehinnom
וּמִיָּד אָתָא אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
and immediately Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him, comes
and for them it is called "the fire of Gehinnom,"
as they said in the Gemara (Pesachim 54a)
for with Yisrael the letter kuf signifies kadosh,
שֶׁנֶּהְפַּךְ הַק׳ אֲתַר דְּגֵיהִנֹּם לְק׳ קָדוֹשׁ.
in which the kuf of the place of Gehinnom was turned into the kuf of kadosh.
"When did all the ends of the earth see
In the days of Mordechai and Esther."
That is, even those far from Hashem,
who are called "all the ends of the earth,"
saw then and recognized the miracle,
that it was the salvation of Hashem, which was reversed:
they merited to carry out the obliteration of Amalek,
מַה שֶּׁלֹּא הָיָה אֶפְשָׁר בִּלְעֲדֵי הַגְּזֵירָה
which would not have been possible without the decree —
to seek to destroy and kill the Amalekites, as is understood.
וְכֵן הָיָה שֶׁנֶּהְפַּךְ ק׳ אַתְרָא דְּגֵיהִנֹּם
And so it was that the kuf of the place of Gehinnom,
לְק׳ קָדוֹשׁ שֶׁמּוֹרֶה עַל בְּחִינַת חָכְמָה
was turned into the kuf of kadosh, which indicates the aspect of Chochmah,
מַאֲמַר יְהִי אוֹר [בְּרֵאשִׁית א, ג] כָּאָמוּר.
the utterance "Let there be light" (Bereishis 1:3), as was said.
In Nissan, too, there were miracles
and on the contrary, great miracles;
רַק אָז לֹא נֶהְפַּךְ הַגְּזֵירָה לִישׁוּעָה
only then the decree was not turned into salvation,
which is not so in Adar,
where the decree itself was turned into salvation
וְזֶה הוֹרָאַת אוֹת קוֹ״ף כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
and this is the meaning of the letter kuf, as mentioned above.
Haman rejoiced when the lot fell on Adar,
the month in which Moshe died,
and he thought that it was the time
for the extinguishing of the light, chas v'shalom;
but he did not know that in it Moshe was born
שֶׁכְּשֶׁנּוֹלַד נִתְמַלֵּא הַבַּיִת אוֹר [סוֹטָה יב, א]
that when he was born the house was filled with light (Sotah 12a),
and he brought down the Torah, which is light,
who were called "a holy nation" at Matan Torah;
and to this the kuf points.
Therefore we increase joy in it,
and "let him present himself in Adar, whose mazal is strong,"
שֶׁהוּא חָזָק שֶׁלֹּא יִבָּטֵל לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד
for it is strong and will not be nullified forever and ever:
"Hu made us, and to the Aleph are we";
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר עִבְדוּ אֶת ה׳ בְּשִׂמְחָה:
as it says, "Serve Hashem with joy."

paragraphs.text: Psalms 149:2 — “Let Israel rejoice in its Maker; let the children of Zion exult in their King.”

rich.text: Psalms 149:2
— “Let Israel rejoice in its Maker; let the children of Zion exult in their King.”

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Tanya, Likkutei Amarim 33:4–6 — “When a person considers this deeply, his heart rejoices and his soul exults, even singing out with all his heart, soul and strength in this faith, for it is actual closeness to God. This is the whole purpose of man and of the creation of all the upper and lower worlds: that He should have this dwelling below. How great is the joy of an ordinary person of low station when a flesh-and-blood king draws near and comes to lodge and live with him in his house! How infinitely more so when the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, draws near and dwells with him. This is why we praise and thank Him every morning: 'Fortunate are we; how good is our portion … and how beautiful our inheritance.' As one rejoices over an enormous inheritance for which he did not toil, so, infinitely more, should we rejoice over our forefathers' bequest: God's true unity, that even here below there is nothing besides Him.”

paragraphs.text: Connection: Tanya makes the transition from accepting kingship to joy concrete: recognizing the King's nearness is itself a privilege that gives joy, even before measuring one's accomplishments. Rav Tzadok locates this joy in Israel's bond to its divine root. The analogy and the inherited character of this bond explain why the heavenly yoke can produce exultation rather than the burden associated here with human rule.

paragraphs.text: Berakhot 30b — “Abaye was sitting before Rabbah, who saw that he was very cheerful. He said, ‘But it is written, ‘Rejoice with trembling’!’ He answered, ‘I am wearing tefillin.’ Rabbi Yirmeyah was sitting before Rabbi Zeira, who saw that he was very cheerful. He said, ‘But it is written, ‘In all toil there is gain’!’ He answered, ‘I am wearing tefillin.’” The Gemara gives two encounters. Rav Tzadok reads the shared reply as recognition of the divine sovereignty and attachment represented by tefillin.

paragraphs.text: Psalms 100:2-3 — “Serve the Lord with joy; come before Him with song. Know that the Lord is God: He made us, and we are His—His people and the flock of His pasture.” The written consonants in verse 3 give ve-lo with aleph, “and not we”; the traditional reading gives ve-lo with vav, “and we are His.” Rav Tzadok develops the two spellings together.

paragraphs.text: Zohar III, 290a (Idra Zuta) — “In the teaching of the school of Rav Yeiva the Elder, the totality of everything, Ze‘ir Anpin, is called ‘You’; Atika Kadisha, which is concealed, is called ‘He.’ This is fitting. Now we call the place where a beginning is found ‘You’: although it is concealed, from it there is a beginning, and it is called Father.... This Father issues from Atika Kadisha, as it is written, ‘Wisdom—from Ayin shall it be found.’ Therefore He is not apprehended.”

paragraphs.text: Zohar I, 120b (Vayera) — “Whenever troubles befall Israel, ‘lo’ is written with aleph but read with vav, because the Holy One, blessed be He, is with them in their distress. ‘Lo’ with aleph signifies a still higher place. Although anger and distress do not exist in that place, Israel’s distress reaches there above. ‘Lo’ with aleph is as in, ‘He made us, ve-lo anachnu’: it is written with aleph and read with vav.” The passage begins from Isaiah 63:9 and then explicitly compares Psalm 100:3. Rav Tzadok applies that higher, concealed level to the joy of belonging to God.

paragraphs.text: Asarah Maamarot, Maamar Chikur HaDin I:1 — “Contemplation of His attributes is the ultimate good, and ‘Your splendor upon their children’ is like the merit of fathers becoming the mazal of their children.... ‘May the pleasantness of the Lord our God be upon us’ is our primal mazal, which does not depend on merit at all. He prepared for the house of Israel abundant goodness and mighty kindness, with the generous hand of the supreme King who benefits all. ‘The work of our hands’ is the merit renewed day by day: ‘Establish it upon us,’ to add strength to our mazal in every generation.” The chapter says that ancestral merit becomes the children’s mazal. Rav Tzadok formulates this relationship as the father’s soul being the son’s mazal; that exact formula was not found verbatim in the retrieved chapter.

paragraphs.text: Ritva on Yoma 54b — “When gentiles entered the Sanctuary, they found the cherubim intertwined. Rabbi ben Maush raised the difficulty that Bava Batra says their faces were toward one another only when Israel performed God’s will. Some answer that the latter refers to Moses’ cherubim, while here it refers to the cherubim depicted upon the walls, which were always intertwined. But this is difficult: how, then, did they display the depicted cherubim to demonstrate Israel’s belovedness before God? The correct explanation, as Rabbi Eliyahu Mizrachi explained, is that these too were now intertwined by a miracle; but it was a miracle for harm, in order to expose their nakedness.” Rav Tzadok accepts the question and develops a different explanation: Israel’s repentance at the destruction renewed their attachment to God.

paragraphs.text: Bava Batra 99a — “How did they stand? Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Elazar disagree: one says, ‘Their faces were toward one another’; the other says, ‘Their faces were toward the house.’ According to the view that their faces were toward one another, does Scripture not say, ‘Their faces were toward the house’? There is no difficulty: one case is when Israel performs the Omnipresent’s will; the other is when Israel does not perform His will.”

paragraphs.text: Jerusalem Talmud, Berachos 2:4; cf. Eikhah Rabbah 1:51 — “There was a Jew who stood plowing. His ox lowed before him. An Arab passed and heard its voice. He said, ‘Jew, Jew! Unharness your ox and unfasten your plow, for the Temple has been destroyed.’ It lowed a second time. He said, ‘Jew, Jew! Harness your ox and fasten your plow, for the King Messiah has been born.’ He asked, ‘What is his name?’ He answered, ‘Menachem.’” The same story is present in Eikhah Rabbah 1:51, after its opening Doeg narrative and subsequent expositions. Both original witnesses place the birth of consolation beside the very announcement of destruction.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Maharsha, Chiddushei Aggados, Megillah 13b — “His death on the seventh of Adar is partly explicit in the verses, but his birth on the seventh of Adar is only a derashah of the sages … and Haman did not know this derashah.” Maharsha explains why Haman could not know. Moshe's birth in Adar is known only through the sages' teaching, so Haman read the month as one of loss alone.
